messages:
devon: Heads-up — we've seen a pattern of rapid spot GPU evictions in us-west1 this morning during batch retrains.  ~30% of nodes got taken in 10m windows.

alina: Yep saw it. metric: spot_evictions_per_min spiked to 18 at 09:12. Impact: queued jobs backfilled onto small on-demand pool -> latency spikes for inference canaries.

marco: Dumped recent allocation map: most evictions hit price-optimized pools. capacity-optimized pools remained steadier.

julia: Interesting. Are we still using price-optimized as default for low-cost clusters?

devon: Default for non-urgent training yes. But inference-batch and realtime fall back to mixed-pool config. The issue is some regional pools advertise cheaper price but are volatile.

alina: Proposal: flip default for all GPU procurement to capacity-first for primary regions (us-west1/us-east1/europe-west1), keep a small price-optimized bucket for opportunistic work only.

marco: Agree. Also propose a 5% warm-buffer of on-demand (or reserved/dedicated) instances per cluster to absorb short eviction bursts. That prevents immediate fallback across regions.

devon: +1. Also need smarter failover rules to avoid cross-region spills that cause egress charges. Current policy blindly routes to next-available region.

julia: Can we update routing policy: prefer same-region capacity-optimized -> same-cloud other-region capacity-optimized -> price-optimized in-region -> price-optimized cross-region (last resort). Annotate route with estimated egress cost.

marco: We should also add quick model fallback: when eviction rate > 5/min for 2m, switch non-critical jobs to quantized model variant (smaller memory, same accuracy) to reduce GPU footprint.

alina: That needs a short TTL to revert when stability returns. + add a metric for "model_fallback_active" so Optimize dashboards can correlate cost savings.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure bid strategy toggle is behind feature flag -> canary 5% clusters -> health checks (eviction_rate, tail_latency, egress_cost) -> rollback on >3 failures in 15m.

devon: Draft playbook for ops: 1) enable capacity-first in account-level procurement config 2) set warm-buffer=5% 3) set route-preference order as julia suggested 4) enable quantized fallback for opportunistic workloads 5) monitor evictions and egress.

marco: Quick config snippet for the procurement flag:
```yaml
procurement_policy: 
  default_pool_priority: ["capacity-optimized", "on-demand-warm", "price-optimized"]
  warm_buffer_percent: 5
  cross_region_egress_threshold_usd: 10  # per minute threshold to avoid cross-region failover
```

julia: Nice. Add a cooldown window for Spot bids: if eviction spike detected, automatically increase max-bid by 10% for 3m to try and stabilize a portion of the pool. But only in price-optimized pools.

alina: Need to be careful on spending. Add a guard: total extra-bid spend per region capped to X% of hourly budget. Also surface projected spend in console.

devon: Ops runbook step for oncall: if evictions persist > 12m and fallbacks fail, trigger emergency capacity step: spin reserved nodes (if available) or temporarily increase dedicated throughput. Notify product owners.

marco: For experiments: canary on us-west1 with 10 clusters, track metrics for 2h. Experiment variants: A) capacity-only B) mixed with 5% warm-buffer C) mixed + bid-up on spike.

julia: Metrics to watch: evictions/min, tail_latency_99, queued_jobs, cross_region_egress_usd, model_fallback_rate, token_cost_delta.

devon: Who wants to own the canary? I can kick off infra changes and monitor for the first 2 hours.

alina: I'll wire the dashboard panels and add alerting rules.

marco: I'll implement the procurement_policy config and the automatic bid-up patch.

sre-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance in us-west1 at 23:00 UTC may change capacity patterns. Keep that in mind for canary timing.

julia: Also add a quick smoke test: run 100 small inference requests across nodes after rollout to ensure KV cache warmups behave.

devon: Sounds good. Plan: implement today, canary tomorrow 08:00 UTC, 2h observation, then roll to remaining clusters if stable.

alina: :thumbsup: I'll create the feature-flag and console card.

marco: FYI — I'll add a short note to procurement docs about region egress tradeoffs and a recommended default (capacity-first in primary regions).

devon: Thanks all. Filing follow-ups: #1 create feature flag (alina) #2 implement config + bid-up (marco) #3 dashboards/alerts (alina) #4 canary orchestration (devon).

ops-bot: action-created: procurement-policy-change (owner: marco) | canary-job (owner: devon) | dashboard-ticket (owner: alina)

julia: If anything goes sideways ping me and product-alerts channel.

devon: Closing thread — will post canary results in this thread tomorrow.
